autopsy.top1_name: Abstract reads as one coherent argument, not a fragment list
autopsy.top1_instruction: Score 10 if the abstract flows as one integrated narrative (problem, insight, method, validation) with clear logical connectives. Score 5 if it is readable but reads as a loosely connected sequence of claims. Score 0 if it reads as a fragmented list of disconnected technical assertions/results, or relies on gimmicks such as spelling out an acronym letter-by-letter in place of plain description.
autopsy.concept_definition: Title is specific/accurate; abstract is concise and aligned with methods/results/conclusions; keywords/subjects are appropriate and, where applicable, use standardized/controlled vocabularies for discoverability.

autopsy.concept: TRIPOD adherence for prediction model studies
autopsy.top1_instruction: Score 10 if the method is validated via a real operational deployment, a competitive leaderboard/challenge win, or application to genuine external (non-benchmark-curated) data (e.g. real sensor/rover/production data). Score 5 if the paper merely gestures at 'real-world applicability' without concrete deployment evidence. Score 0 if all validation is confined to standard academic benchmark splits.
autopsy.concept_definition: Prediction model studies (development/validation/update) comply with TRIPOD, stating study type, data sources, modelling/validation methods, and reporting performance (e.g., calibration, discrimination) with uncertainty.

autopsy.top1_instruction: Score 10 when the work reveals how data quality, structure, labeling, or sampling governs the task and turns that insight into a principled intervention; score 0 when data are treated as interchangeable inputs or a dataset is introduced without a substantive insight.
autopsy.concept_definition: Datasets include rich metadata (FAIR‑aligned), composition/collection details and stewardship plans, intended uses/limitations, ethical/privacy constraints, and guidance to avoid harmful or inappropriate use.

autopsy.concept: Discussion and conclusions — interpretation and implications
autopsy.top1_name: Stated mechanistic hypothesis for why the method works
autopsy.top1_instruction: Score 10 if the abstract offers an explicit causal/mechanistic hypothesis for why the proposed technique should improve results (not just that it does), stated as a reasoned claim about mechanism. Score 5 if a mechanism is gestured at but not clearly articulated. Score 0 if the abstract only reports that a method 'improves performance' with no account of why.
autopsy.concept_definition: Findings are interpreted in light of objectives, prior evidence, and theory; alternative explanations and limitations are considered; conclusions are clear and appropriately restrained; practical/scientific implications and synthesis are articulated.
